title: Binary Optimization with Complex Constraints via Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization
authors: Andres Ruiz, Soumyadip Ghosh, Stefan Woerner
abstract: We show that a class of binary optimization problems with complex non-quadratic objectives or constraints can be reformulated as multi-objective quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problems. When the objective and constraints depend on a small number of quadratic features and are monotone with respect to their preferred directions, at least one globally optimal solution lies in the Pareto set of the associated MO-QUBO. This enables the constraints to be evaluated classically on Pareto-optimal candidates rather than encoded as penalties. We demonstrate the approach for binary portfolio optimization under a Conditional Value-at-Risk constraint. Using Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization on an illustrative 100-asset instance, we approximate the mean-variance Pareto front using an IBM Quantum computer and derive mean-CVaR fronts through classical post-processing. The hardware results recover the overall structure of the classical front and yield near-optimal feasible portfolios for different risk bounds.
summary: This work reformulates complex, constrained binary optimization problems into Multi-Objective QUBOs solvable via quantum computation. By applying Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization (QAMOO) to portfolio selection, the authors successfully approximate the mean-variance and mean-CVaR Pareto fronts. The results show that the quantum approach yields near-optimal portfolios that closely match established classical benchmarks.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing binary problems with complex, non-quadratic constraints by reformulating them into Multi-Objective Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (MO-QUBO) problems.
main_result: The proposed quantum approach, using QAMOO, successfully approximates the Pareto front for portfolio optimization (mean-variance and mean-CVaR) and yields near-optimal feasible portfolios when compared against classical benchmarks.
method: The methodology involves transforming constrained optimization into an MO-QUBO, solving for the Pareto set using QAMOO on a quantum computer, and then classically evaluating the original non-quadratic constraints on the resulting candidates.
model_or_system: The model is binary portfolio selection ($x \in \{0, 1\}^n$) aiming to optimize expected return ($\mu^T x$) subject to a Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) constraint, which is non-quadratic.
key_observables: Pareto front structure, Hypervolume (HV) indicator, Expected Return, CVaR values for $\alpha = 90\%, 95\%, 99\%$.
important_parameters: Number of assets ($n$), risk aversion level ($\alpha$), and QAOA circuit parameters ($ eta_l, \gamma_l$).
main_assumptions: The reduction relies on the objective and constraints being monotone with respect to the induced dominance order; global optimality is not guaranteed if only an approximation of the Pareto set is found.
figures_summary: Figures compare the sampled Pareto fronts (mean-variance and mean-CVaR) from QAMOO against classical references ($\epsilon$-CM, WSM), showing close recovery of the front structure. Figure 2 specifically plots the expected-return gap between the two methods.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical framework for reformulating constrained optimization into MO-QUBOs. It then applies this to portfolio optimization, detailing the use of QAMOO on quantum hardware, followed by extensive comparison with classical methods and robustness checks.
why_interesting: It demonstrates a concrete application of quantum optimization algorithms (QAMOO) to a highly relevant financial problem (portfolio optimization) involving complex, non-quadratic constraints, bridging quantum computation with quantitative finance.
